Without Eastern Galicia (to the General Government), Chernigov, Kharkov and the Donets Basin (military governance), the Crimea (military control) and the Romanian-occupied south-west

predecessors.note: Soviet Ukraine west and south of the military zone; Eastern Galicia 'was transferred to the control of the General Government following a Hitler decree' (the general-government dossier). Cliopatria's Nazi Germany 1942 shape draws occupied Ukraine inside the Reich; this dossier gives it its own outline.

land.text: 'In 1943 and 1944, the Red Army liberated most of territory of the Reichskommissariat in its advance westwards'; the Soviets 'reclaim most of the Ukrainian SSR'

successors.note: Formal disestablishment 10 November 1944, three months after the last land was lost.

land.text: 'On 28 July 1944, the Red Army occupied the last part of the Reichskommissariat Ukraine in Brest'

successors.note: Brest, in Belarus, was the last piece.

capitals.name: Rovno (Rivne)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital: Kiev (de jure) Rovno (de facto)'. Erich Koch ruled from Rovno; Kiev was the capital on paper.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no row for the Reichskommissariat. Infobox area 340,000 km2 against 341,000 km2 for the fourteen oblasts alone (ratio 1.00); the Brest circle adds about 11,000 km2 more, so the spec is about 3% over. The page lists the Generalbezirke but not their borders; the oblast reading is mine. The Crimea-Taurida district was under military control (civil administration only for Taurien from September 1942) and Eastern Galicia was transferred to the General Government.

correction.text: the right bank after the Soviet crossing of the Dnieper and the fall of Kiev and Zhytomyr: Cherkasy, Kirovohrad, Vinnytsya, Khmelnytskyi, Rivne, Volyn, Mykolaiv, Kherson and Brest

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for year-end 1943: the Battle of the Dnieper (26 August - 23 December 1943) and the Kiev Strategic Offensive (3-13 November) took the left bank and Kiev, and Zhitomir fell on 31 December (Dnieper–Carpathian page). The shape is the right bank still held on 1 January 1944; during 1943 the ledger gives the losses month by month.

correction.text: the right bank after the Soviet crossing of the Dnieper and the fall of Kiev and Zhytomyr: Cherkasy, Kirovohrad, Vinnytsya, Khmelnytskyi, Rivne, Volyn, Mykolaiv, Kherson and Brest

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the last year: the shape at 1 January 1944 (same as year-end 1943); the Dnieper–Carpathian offensive took it piece by piece through 1944 (ledger), the last part (Brest) on 28 July 1944, and the Reichskommissariat was formally dissolved on 10 November 1944.

region.text: the six Generalbezirke of 1941 read as modern oblasts: Shitomir (Zhytomyr), Kiew (Kiev), Nikolajew (Nikolayev), Wolhynien und Podolien (Volhynia and Podolia; Luzk), Dnjepropetrowsk (Dnepropetrovsk) and the Brest area; infobox area 340,000 km2. Without Eastern Galicia (to the General Government), Chernigov, Kharkov and the Donets Basin (military governance), the Crimea (military control) and the Romanian-occupied south-west

ledger.note: 20 August 1941: Hitler establishes the Reichskommissariat Ukraine. 'On 20 August, Hitler established the Reichskommissariat Ukraine' (infobox 'Established: 20 August 1941'; 'On 17 July 1941, Hitler issued a Führer decree defining the administration of the newly-occupied Eastern territories'). The page gives the Generalbezirke, not borders.

region.text: the Reichskommissariat under German civil administration

ledger.note: 1 September 1941: German civil administration begins. Infobox 'Implement civil administration: 1 September 1941' ('from noon on 1 September'); area 'Total: 340,000 km2', population '1941: 37,000,000'.

September 1942: the Taurien district goes to civil administration. The page lists Generalbezirk 'Krym-Taurien (Crimea- Taurida; Melitopol)' and says of the units scheduled for incorporation 'Only the first of these saw transfer to civil administration in September 1942'; Kharkov and the other eastern units 'never' transferred. Most of the Taurida mainland is already inside the oblasts of the 1941 shape, so the change is small.

region.text: the left bank of the Dnieper and Kiev, the ground of the Battle of the Dnieper

ledger.note: 26 August 1943: the Battle of the Dnieper begins on the left bank. 'The operation began on 26 August 1943'; 'On 15 September 1943, Hitler ordered Army Group South to retreat to the Dnieper defence line'.

region.text: the Poltava region, taken in the advance to the Dnieper

ledger.note: September 1943: Poltava falls. 'After two days of violent urban warfare, the Poltava garrison was overcome'; the page gives no date, only that 'Towards the end of September 1943, Soviet forces reached the lower part of the Dnieper'. Confidence 1: the month bridges a silence.
10-14 October 1943: the Zaporizhia offensive. The page lists 'Zaporizhia Offensive 10–14 October 1943' but not the capture date.
3-13 November 1943: the Kiev Strategic Offensive. The page lists 'Kiev Strategic Offensive 3–13 November 1943' but does not date the capture of Kiev itself.
December 1943: the Dnepropetrovsk offensive ends. The page lists 'Dnepropetrovsk Offensive 23 October – 23 December 1943' and gives the battle's end as 23 December 1943.

region.text: the left bank of the Dnieper and Kiev, the ground of the Battle of the Dnieper

ledger.note: 23 December 1943: the Battle of the Dnieper ends. Infobox '26 August 1943 – 23 December 1943'; 'Soviet forces controlled a bridgehead 300 kilometers wide and up to 80 kilometers deep in some places'.

region.text: the right bank of the Dnieper and Volhynia-Podolia, the ground of the Dnieper–Carpathian offensive

ledger.note: 24 December 1943: the Dnieper–Carpathian offensive begins on the right bank. 'The offensive was launched on December 24, 1943, by Vatutin's 1st Ukrainian Front'.
29-31 December 1943: Korosten and Zhytomyr fall. 'Korosten fell on December 29, and Zhitomir followed on December 31.'
5-16 January 1944: Kirovohrad is taken. 'The most important result of the operation was the liberation of Kirovograd'; the page dates the Kirovograd Offensive 5–16 January 1944.

27 January - 11 February 1944: the Rovno–Lutsk offensive takes the Reichskommissariat's capital region. The page lists 'Rovno–Lutsk Offensive (27 January 1944 – 11 February 1944)' but gives no capture date for Rovno.

10 March 1944: Uman falls. 'On March 10, the 2nd Ukrainian Front destroyed two Panzer Corps by capturing them at the fall of Uman'. The Cherkasy oblast is read from Uman; the Korsun pocket is not on the pages.

region.text: Vinnytsia, Khmelnytskyi and the south of the Reichskommissariat up to the Bug

ledger.note: April 1944: the rest of right-bank Ukraine is retaken. The page says 'Vinnitsa, Volyn, Zhytomir, Kiev, Kirovohrad, Rivne, Khmelnytskyi and parts of Poltava Oblasts, and the Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic were taken by the Red Army' and that the German troops 'began to fall back from the Bug' on 28 March; it gives no day for Mykolaiv or Kherson and ends the offensive on 6 May 1944. Confidence 1: the month is a bridge.

region.text: the right bank of the Dnieper and Volhynia-Podolia, the ground of the Dnieper–Carpathian offensive

ledger.note: 28 July 1944: the Red Army occupies the last part. 'On 28 July 1944, the Red Army occupied the last part of the Reichskommissariat Ukraine in Brest.'

28 July 1944: Brest, the last piece, is lost. 'On 28 July 1944, the Red Army occupied the last part of the Reichskommissariat Ukraine in Brest'; the infobox adds 'Remainder part of Generalbezirk Weißruthenien: 25 February 1944' (the page does not explain it).

region.text: the last land of the Reichskommissariat

ledger.note: July 1944: German civil rule ends with the loss of Brest. 'In 1943 and 1944, the Red Army liberated most of territory of the Reichskommissariat in its advance westwards.'

region.text: the Reichskommissariat, then reduced to a name

ledger.note: 10 November 1944: the Reichskommissariat Ukraine is formally dissolved. 'Reichskommissariat Ukraine was officially dissolved on 10 November 1944' (infobox 'Formal disestablishment: 10 November 1944').

wars.name: Battle of the Dnieper

zones.text: the left bank of the Dnieper and Kiev, the ground of the Battle of the Dnieper

wars.outcome: The Red Army crosses the Dnieper (first bridgehead 22 September 1943) and takes the left bank and Kiev; the battle ends on 23 December 1943 with a bridgehead 300 km wide.
wars.note: Dated 26 August - 23 December 1943; the Zaporizhia (10-14 October), Kiev (3-13 November) and Dnepropetrovsk (23 October - 23 December) offensives are its parts.

wars.name: Dnieper–Carpathian offensive

zones.text: the right bank of the Dnieper and Volhynia-Podolia, the ground of the Dnieper–Carpathian offensive

wars.outcome: Launched 24 December 1943; Korosten and Zhytomyr fall at the end of December, Kirovograd in January, the Rovno-Lutsk sector in February, Uman on 10 March, Odessa on 10 April 1944; the Red Army reaches the June 1941 border and the Carpathians.
wars.note: The infobox ends the offensive on 6 May 1944; the Reichskommissariat's last piece, Brest, falls on 28 July 1944 (Reichskommissariat Ukraine page).

certainty.note: The page lists Generalbezirke without borders, and the eastern edge is a military-governance boundary; the western edge against the General Government (East Galicia) is a decree line. From autumn 1943 the edge is the moving front.

sources.title: Reichskommissariat Ukraine

sources.title: Battle of the Dnieper
sources.note: 26 August - 23 December 1943; offensive dates for Zaporizhia, Kiev, Dnepropetrovsk; silent on the capture days of Kiev, Kharkov, Zhytomyr.

sources.title: Dnieper–Carpathian offensive
sources.note: 24 December 1943 start, Korosten 29 and Zhitomir 31 December, Kirovograd 5-16 January, Rovno–Lutsk 27 January - 11 February, Uman 10 March, Odessa 10 April 1944.

notes: Cliopatria lacks the Reichskommissariat; the nazi-germany dossier draws occupied Ukraine from Cliopatria's 1942 shape as occupation of ukrainian-soviet-socialist-republic, so the overlap should be settled by the rendering step. Oblast boundaries stand in for the Generalbezirke (the page names them but not their limits), and the pages are silent on: Kiev's capture day (6 November 1943 is not on the pages), Rovno's capture (2 February 1944 is not on the pages), Mykolaiv and Kherson, the Korsun pocket and Poltava. Military-governed land (Chernigov, Kharkov, Donets Basin, Crimea) is outside the shape; Reichskommissariat Ostland (the Baltic and Belarus) is a separate state that needs its own dossier; Eastern Galicia is in general-government; the Romanian Transnistria Governorate is a separate counterpart that nobody has yet. The infobox line 'Remainder part of Generalbezirk Weißruthenien: 25 February 1944' is unexplained on the page.
